A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ridgeless least-squares research. Their text, equations, figures, references, and appendices are readable and support comparison despite the revised title and substantial theoretical reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original Monte Carlo simulations with autoregressive and clustered errors, including empirical variance estimates and overparameterization curves in Figures 1–4.

after.justification: v2 retains these simulations and adds empirical prediction-risk variance and bias results in Figures 1–4.

M1.justification: Both versions use the same minimum-norm least-squares estimator computed through the Moore–Penrose inverse. v2's explicit constrained-minimization formulation does not change the estimation procedure.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same Gaussian-design linear-regression simulations with autoregressive and clustered errors and the same overparameterization scenarios. Prediction risk adds measurements on retained simulations. The removed heteroskedastic examples in Appendix A were theoretical examples, not evaluated datasets or scenarios.

E2.justification: Neither version benchmarks alternative estimators. Both compare simulated quantities with finite-sample theoretical expressions and asymptotic reference curves; the added prediction-risk expressions do not introduce a competing estimation method.

E3.justification: v2 adds covariance-weighted prediction variance and bias as evaluation quantities. Existing settings remain: n=50, p=100 for Figure 1; n=20, p=40 for Figure 2; and fixed n=50 with varying p/n for Figure 3. No revision to the retained simulation protocol is documented.

E4.justification: v2 extends the existing analyses to prediction risk: Figure 4 checks insensitivity to randomized within-cluster covariances, and Figure 3 examines behavior as p/n increases. These supplement the corresponding estimation-risk analyses already present in v1.

E5.justification: Figures 1 and 2 retain 100 design-matrix samples and 100 error samples per design realization. Neither version adds seed reporting, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty estimates for the Monte Carlo results.

E6.justification: Figures 1, 2, and 4 add empirical prediction-variance contours and corresponding theoretical values. Figure 3 adds prediction-variance and prediction-bias curves across p/n. These substantially expand reported outcomes and extend the reported trace-factorization and variance-descent findings; the earlier estimation-risk panels are retained.

T1.justification: v2 adds prediction-variance Theorem 3.2 with a singular-vector/Haar-averaging proof, weighted random-effects Assumption 4.2, and prediction-risk Corollary 4.1. It removes v1's conditional bounds, Theorem 2.2, covariance-dependence relaxation, and Appendix A examples, while strengthening error independence assumptions. Estimation-risk formulas and asymptotics largely survive renumbering. The new prediction-bias derivation in Equation (5) contains an invalid matrix-square step for general anisotropic covariance.

C1.justification: The title, abstract, and introduction expand the principal claims from estimation MSE to both prediction and estimation risks, including trace-based variance characterization for both. v1's two-part contribution of general conditional bounds and more restrictive unconditional characterization is replaced by an emphasis on exact finite-sample variance factorization.

C2.justification: v2 narrows applicability to errors independent of the design, removing discussion of design-dependent heteroskedasticity and the conditional-bound argument for bias dominance. It extends the trace-only interpretation to prediction variance and newly asserts that prediction bias depends only on rank deficiency under its weighted random-effects assumption.

D1.justification: Appendix B adds a brief instruction to apply the existing Monte Carlo approach analogously to prediction variance. The Gaussian/Haar covariance construction and nested sampling recipe are otherwise retained, with no new code-access, hardware, or runtime information.

R1.justification: The cited works are unchanged. v2 drops v1's explicit assertion that left-spherical symmetry had not been explored for ridgeless estimators and repositions the contribution from an estimation-MSE alternative to a joint finite-sample treatment of prediction and estimation risks.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, research questions, and contribution paragraphs are rewritten. Section 2 becomes a framework section; variance and bias receive separate sections organized by risk type; the former asymptotics section becomes Section 4.2.1. Clustered-error explanations are rewritten, and the former Appendix A content disappears.

P2.justification: Figures 1, 2, and 4 expand from two to four panels, and Figure 3 expands from one to two panels. Prediction results appear above retained estimation results, with revised legends and captions. Figure 3 is now placed after Appendix B begins.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful prediction-variance theory and numerical evidence, but introduces a substantive error into its new full prediction-risk claim. Appendix C's proof of Equation (5) replaces a matrix–transpose product with the square of a generally nonsymmetric matrix. Consequently, the claimed rank-only prediction bias and Corollary 4.1 fail for general anisotropic covariance under the stated assumptions. v1's unweighted-bias derivation avoids this error. The damage to a central mathematical claim outweighs the expanded coverage.
